results.corrected_extracted: Product-level data (Fig 9A legend: Hybrid 7,306, Indica 2,944, Sativa 1,813, None 1,338). Category shares (Fig 9B): overall Hybrid 60.6%, Indica 24.4%, Sativa 15.0%; Cluster I 64.1, 24.8 and 11.1%; Cluster II 57.1, 27.4 and 15.6%; Cluster III (terpinolene-rich) 55.8, 13.3 and 30.9%. Only Cluster III was reported as differing from the overall shares (χ² 22.2, P < 0.0001); Clusters I and II reported as not different. Purple Punch: 96% of products in Cluster I against 61.8% under shuffling. The authors write that even the single most over-represented name in each cluster (Dogwalker OG, 100% in Cluster I; Blue Dream, 88.5% in Cluster II; Dutch Treat, 85.9% in Cluster III) is not perfectly associated with one chemotype, and that products under each name vary within the cluster. Editors' calculation: the χ² formula applied to the Fig 9B percentages as if they were counts gives 22.3 (Cluster III), 1.2 (I) and 0.6 (II); product counts per cluster are not given, so the tests cannot be redone.

results.note: The 'not perfectly associated' sentence (2nd paragraph) concerns Dogwalker OG (100%), Blue Dream and Dutch Treat, not Purple Punch; Purple Punch figures are on p. 14. Fig 9 values (300 dpi) and χ² recalculation (22.3, 1.2, 0.6) confirmed.

results.corrected_extracted: Measurements came from six laboratories using methods that may not be standardized (cannabinoids by HPLC with diode-array or UV detection; terpenes by GC-FID or GC-MS, reported in % weight, ppm or mg/g); the authors cannot tell whether regional differences reflect real variation or laboratory methods; testing is not standardized nationally, so the main analyses used only compounds measured by every laboratory. Caveats listed by the authors: pooled data from different states, no genotype or growing conditions, compounds not measured everywhere, different state rules, hemp not included.
results.note: Source restricts the common-compound list to 'our main analyses' (S1 Fig shows every cannabinoid by region). All else confirmed, including Table 1 methods and units.

N.J. is the only author listed for conceptualization, investigation, supervision and validation, and is also listed for data curation, methodology, project administration and writing.

results.corrected_extracted: Terpenes are described as responsible for cannabis's odours; consumers often believe Indica-labelled products are sedating and Sativa-labelled ones energizing; whether different cannabinoid and terpene ratios consistently give different subjective effects is stated to be unknown. No effects were measured. The Discussion concludes that the Indica/Hybrid/Sativa system does not reliably distinguish samples by chemical content, that it is therefore highly unlikely to indicate systematically different effects, and that strain names may be better markers of chemistry than the categories but are far from ideal.

results.corrected_extracted: Ten coffee shops in Amsterdam, Utrecht, Groningen and Maastricht, each visited twice about two months apart; 1 g each of Amnesia (described as a Sativa-dominant type) and White Widow (an Indica-dominant type), chosen because both were generally available at all locations throughout the year; 5 of 40 planned purchases unavailable, leaving 18 Amnesia and 17 White Widow samples; 28 compounds present at a mean of at least 0.5 mg/g, quantified by GC-FID in one laboratory.

Table 1 rows 3, 6 and 26 read on a 300-dpi rendering; PC1 27.2%, PC2 17.0%, THC values and 'no significant difference' without a test confirmed at PDF p. 5.

results.corrected_extracted: Three of the samples bought had the chemical fingerprint of the other cultivar; the authors assumed mix-ups at the coffee shop and excluded them, conceding that they might be genuine specimens, which would widen the variation within each cultivar (the text and the figure legend disagree on which way the mix-ups went). Relative standard deviations above 25% were found for 14 compounds across purchases (by the editors' count of Table 1, 14 compound-and-cultivar pairs, 13 distinct compounds, beta-caryophyllene exceeding 25% in both cultivars, reading the misaligned gamma-selinene row, whose 34.6 is printed in Amnesia's SD column, as Amnesia's RSD). The dotted group outlines in Fig 2 were drawn by the authors and signify no test.
results.note: Recount on the rendered Table 1: 8 White Widow + 6 Amnesia = 14 pairs only if the shifted gamma-selinene value is read as Amnesia's RSD; read literally, 13. Rest confirmed.
PDF p. 6: resemblances, lineages, 'closer to Amnesia' and the low-terpene explanation confirmed; 'triplicate analyses of one batch' is in the Fig 2 legend beneath panel a.

results.corrected_extracted: Popular descriptions of Sativa effects (uplifting, energetic) and Indica effects (body relaxation, sleep) are summarized from a popular book, and the authors state it has not been properly confirmed whether such descriptions relate to the Indica-Sativa distinction or to any chemical classification; no effects were measured. The pharmacy varieties came from the official Dutch grower, Bedrocan BV; each cultivar's Sativa or Indica background was taken from a seed company's website (Sensi Seed Bank); the first author has been employed by Bedrocan BV as head of research and development since February 2011. No test statistic or p value is reported for any comparison: differences called significant in the text come without a named test, and Bedrocan is called significantly different only because it lies outside the PCA plot's 95% confidence ellipse.

Author Contributions (p. 28) list N.J., the Leafly employee, alone for conceptualization, investigation, supervision and validation and also for data curation and methodology; affiliations_note mentions only conception, supervision and validation, and the overlap with the statement that Leafly had no role in design or data collection and analysis is worth recording.

Two of the earlier label studies in the replication timeline share authors with this paper (ref. 34, Jikomes & Zoorob 2018; ref. 46, Vergara, Gaudino, Blank & Keegan 2020), so they are not independent of it.

key_findings.correction: Fig 2a checked at 400 dpi: two closed triangles inside the White Widow group, one closed circle inside the Amnesia group, as the legend says.

Pharmacy varieties: Bedica, derived from an Indica type, closely resembled White Widow, which the authors say would explain their similarity; Bedrobinol, bred from a Haze variety with a large share of Sativa genes, also resembled White Widow, which they call surprising and suggest may reflect its very low terpene content; Bedrocan, from a Jack Herer background described as slightly Sativa-dominant, resembled neither coffee-shop type nor the other pharmacy varieties and lay closer to Amnesia, with myrcene, cis-ocimene and terpinolene at least twice Amnesia's levels. [The lead 'Lineage labels did not predict the pharmacy varieties' chemistry' goes beyond the source: the authors present Bedica and Bedrocan as consistent with their lineage; only Bedrobinol was unexpected.]

Counting the 5 unavailable products and the 3 presumed mix-ups, the authors estimate that, if their experience is representative, in 20% of cases (8 of 40 visits) a buyer would not receive a reliable service at an average coffee shop. [Source says 'reliable service'; five of the eight were unavailability, not a product.]

reporting_issues.correction: issue: unchanged | consequence: The comparison mixes analytical repeatability with batch-to-batch variation and favours the pharmacy products; the earlier study's RSDs are also described as coming from 'a standard batch' of each variety, so they too may reflect within-batch rather than between-batch variation (that study was not read).
Bedrocan's position outside the 95% ellipse can be seen in Fig 2a; the other stated significances cannot be checked.

risk_of_bias.note: Agree with cross-sectional design, JBI-prevalence and overall high.

interpretation_gap.note: Minor agreed. Wording: the paper speculates that Amnesia's lower α-pinene (an anticholinesterase) could fit stronger memory effects, not that α-pinene counters memory effects in Amnesia (PDF p. 4).

missed: Compounds detected in a single sample have Table 1 means of 0.5–1.9 mg/g with no SD (e.g., CBGM 1.9), which suggests means and RSDs were computed over the samples in which a compound was detected rather than over all purchases; the paper does not say how non-detects were handled (editors' inference).
